clue.text: A note on technique that makes good sense

parts.note: C is one of the musical notes A to G
taken as written
science in the sense of a skill or method, as in 'the science of batting'

explanation.surface: A remark about method that turns out to be very sensible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A note' is not a remark but a musical note, C; 'that makes' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Conscience is the inner moral faculty, a sense of right and wrong.

explanation.surface: Someone departed a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: Food left uneaten is 'left over'; to do something over is to do it once more.

explanation.walkthrough: The clue runs on into 4 down: 4 is that answer, a word for a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: To back a motion in a meeting is to support it; a brief moment, like an instant, is a jiffy of time.

parts.note: the second half of a linked pair: the previous clue's word for a moment also means immediate

explanation.definitionFit: Something done at once, such as instant coffee, is ready immediately.

parts.note: née is used before a woman's maiden name to mean born

explanation.surface: Someone came into the world and left it destitute.
explanation.definitionFit: Want or destitution: to be in need is to be poor.

indicators.note: fashions as a verb means shapes or remakes, so the letters are worked into a new form

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Asian styles are being exported abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fashions' reads as a noun, but it is the verb signalling the anagram of ARE SENT; 'out' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe things from the East, especially Asia.

clue.text: Gratified in accepting nothing can cause conflict

parts.note: gratified means satisfied, pleased

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: taken as written
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Being satisfied while having nothing can lead to strife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gratified' reads as describing a person, but it supplies a synonym; 'can cause' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Contention is dispute or strife, a state of conflict.

parts.note: a well-known make of rifle shares its name with a famous English public school and cathedral city

explanation.definitionFit: Winchester is both a historic rifle maker and the name of an old English public school, Winchester College.

explanation.surface: Headgear suited to an antelope.
explanation.definitionFit: A sun helmet worn in India (sola topi) and an African antelope share the name.

indicators.note: something transferable can be moved about, so the letters change places

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Parasites on cattle could pass over to the flock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transferable' signals the anagram of STEERS LICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Leicesters are a breed of long-wooled English sheep.

clue.text: The jerk is positive and arbitrary

parts.note: taken as written
a tic is an involuntary twitch or jerk

explanation.surface: A nervous twitch described as definite but random.
explanation.definitionFit: In logic, thetic means laid down as a statement, dogmatically asserted without proof.

parts.note: a book lover's favourite pastime doubles as the name of a Berkshire town

explanation.definitionFit: Reading is a large town in Berkshire, west of London, and also what a bookish person loves doing.

clue.text: May be near a Trust House serving refreshments

indicators.note: may be signals these letters could be something else once rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A hotel group's establishment may be close to a café.
explanation.walkthrough: 'May be' signals the anagram of NEAR A TRUST. Trust House was a British hotel chain, which feeds the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A restaurant is an establishment that serves meals to customers.

clue.text: Setting aright people in publicity — aright!

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other

parts.note: an ad is publicity for a product
men as people in general
read as A plus right, and a Tory is someone on the political right

explanation.surface: Correcting people in advertising, and doing it properly!
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'aright' splits as A + RIGHT, the right being TORY, Britain's Conservatives.
explanation.definitionFit: Amendatory means serving to amend or correct.

explanation.surface: A novice who is nevertheless thriving.
explanation.definitionFit: A green recruit is a raw beginner; green growth is lush and vigorous.

clue.text: Fix for Argentinian leaders to travel over

parts.note: the leading letters of Argentinian, its first two
to range is to roam across an area

explanation.surface: A plan for South American bosses to tour widely.
explanation.definitionFit: To fix a meeting is to arrange or settle it.

clue.text: A way to walk when one's in drink

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
one is I, so one's (one is) gives I plus S

explanation.surface: The route someone takes home after a few pints.

explanation.definitionFit: An aisle is a passage between rows of seats, for walking along.

explanation.surface: Plan to catch the bus.
explanation.definitionFit: To point a weapon at something is to direct it; a railway service is a common form of mass transit.

explanation.surface: She would throw something away.
explanation.definitionFit: A contraction for 'she would'; to discard or moult, as a snake its skin.

explanation.surface: A taste that is very fresh.
explanation.definitionFit: Peppermint is a herb used for flavour; in mint condition means pristine and unused.

explanation.definitionFit: Merle is an old and poetic name for the common blackbird.

parts.note: not a delay to coal deliveries but a stand that props up burning logs

explanation.definitionFit: An andiron is a metal support for logs in a fireplace.

clue.text: Old queen having just one real failing

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A former monarch with only a single true weakness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failing' reads as a noun, a flaw, but signals the anagram of ONE REAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Eleanor of Aquitaine and Eleanor of Castile were English queens consort.

clue.text: Rating a painter for going up a mountain

explanation.walkthrough: 'going up' turns TAR + A + RA into the mountain; 'for' is a link.

parts.note: taken as written

parts.note: S is south, one of the poles
aid means help

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' reads as a Polish national but is the south pole, S.

clue.text: Devious rationales characteristic of the politician

parts.note: taken as written

clue.text: Some manor men might regard as average

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Certain estate workers might think of something as ordinary.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition took in 'might regard as', which cannot stand for a noun; only 'average' defines, and 'might regard as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The norm is the usual standard, what is typical.

clue.text: Care for the Channel Islands in isolation?
